payload.statement: A computational research laboratory in which bounded AI processes observe research state, propose instruments, and have those instruments computed, measured and challenged before anything counts as a result.

corpus.title: Qur'an — six short surahs (working set)
corpus.sourceStatement: Transcribed in imlaa'i orthography without full tashkeel by the implementing agent, from general knowledge, as a working set so that the laboratory has real Arabic research material on first run. NOT checked against a printed or critical edition. The laboratory treats this corpus as UNVERIFIED_TRANSCRIPTION: engines may compute over it, but no result derived from it may be promoted to CANONICAL or published until a human researcher verifies the text against a named edition and updates sourceVerification and sourceStatement. To replace it, drop in a verified text file with the same shape.

nullModel.description: On each draw the graph is rewired by double-edge swaps, preserving every node degree and the edge-weight multiset, and the same detector is run again on the rewired graph. This asks whether the observed modularity is higher than what this detector finds in a structureless graph of the same shape.

measurements.interpretationGuard: Modularity above the rewiring null means this detector found more community structure in the observed graph than in structureless graphs of the same degree sequence. It does not show that the communities are meaningful, nor that the relation the graph was built from is the right relation to have computed.

nullModel.model: community-label permutation (graph fixed, partition sizes fixed)
nullModel.description: Nodes are randomly reassigned to communities of the same sizes on the same graph. Retained only as a demonstration that this null is too weak for an optimized partition.

measurements.interpretationGuard: CONTROL, NOT A FINDING. This compares the same value against a null that permutes community labels on the observed graph. A modularity-maximizing detector beats that null on structureless data too, so a significant result here is uninformative. It is recorded to make the difference between an appropriate and an inappropriate null model inspectable.

item.subject: Capability gap: morphology.segment_arabic
item.reason: Morphological segmentation (root, pattern, clitics) needs a morphological database or analyser that is not present in this repository. Until it exists, every token-level result here is surface-form only, and any claim phrased in terms of roots is outside what this laboratory can currently compute. (§12, §38)

item.subject: Capability gap: audio.align_recitation
item.reason: Audio is a first-class research domain in §40, but no audio data or alignment model is present. AudioSegment, word alignment and reciter comparison are unimplemented rather than stubbed.

embeddings.method: classical MDS (double centering, power iteration with deflation)
embeddings.basis: distance = 1 − relation weight; pairs with no retained relation are assigned the maximal distance of 1

provenance.notes: Geometry derived from computed relations. Spatial proximity here is a claim to be measured, not an illustration.

nullModel.description: Embedding coordinates are randomly reassigned among loci and the weight–distance correlation is recomputed. This asks whether the geometry carries the relation structure, or whether any layout of these points would score as well.

measurements.interpretationGuard: This measures only whether the embedding preserves the relation weights it was computed from. It says nothing about whether those relations track anything in the text, and a visually striking layout with a poor score is decoration, not evidence.
